:::{#def-half-space}
#### Half-space

Let $\mathcal{H} = \cb{\vx \in \reals^p : \vec{w}^\top \vx + b = 0}$ be a hyperplane (@def-hyperplane).
The two **open half-spaces** of $\mathcal{H}$ are

$$
\mathcal{H}^+ \eqdef \cb{\vx \in \reals^p : \vec{w}^\top \vx + b > 0}
\quad \text{and} \quad
\mathcal{H}^- \eqdef \cb{\vx \in \reals^p : \vec{w}^\top \vx + b < 0}.
$$ {#eq-half-space}

The **closed half-spaces** also include $\mathcal{H}$ itself:
$\mathcal{H}^+ \cup \mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{H}^- \cup \mathcal{H}$.
Every point of $\reals^p$ is in exactly one of $\mathcal{H}^+$, $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{H}^-$,
because the number $\vec{w}^\top \vx + b$ is positive, zero or negative.
The vector $\vec{w}$ points into $\mathcal{H}^+$:
the number $\vec{w}^\top \vx + b$ goes up when $\vx$ moves in the direction $\vec{w}$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}
Replacing $(\vec{w}, b)$ by $(-\vec{w}, -b)$ describes the same hyperplane
but swaps the names $\mathcal{H}^+$ and $\mathcal{H}^-$.
The sign of $\vec{w}^\top \vx + b$ tells you which side of the hyperplane $\vx$ is on.
A linear classifier uses this sign to assign one of two labels.
:::
